record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one improve on brute-force search for the satisfiability problem for Boolean circuits of size 4n on n inputs?

evidence.quote: Can one improve the brute force search for the satisfiability problem on circuits of size 4n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean circuit on n inputs is a directed acyclic graph whose sources are labeled with input variables x_1,...,x_n (or constants), whose internal nodes (gates) are labeled with binary Boolean operations chosen from the full binary basis B_2 (all functions {0,1}^2 -> {0,1}), and which has one designated output node. The size of the circuit is the number of gates. The circuit satisfiability problem (Circuit-SAT) takes as input such a circuit C and asks whether there exists an assignment a in {0,1}^n with C(a) = 1.

Brute-force search solves Circuit-SAT in time 2^n · poly(|C|) by trying every input assignment.

Question: Does there exist a (possibly randomized) algorithm that, given as input a Boolean circuit C over the basis B_2 of size at most 4n on n input variables, decides whether C is satisfiable in time 2^{(1-ε)n} · poly(n) for some absolute constant ε > 0, thereby improving on brute-force search?
artifact.status_search_result: Known improved Circuit-SAT algorithms (e.g., Calabro–Impagliazzo–Paturi and follow-ups) beat brute force for circuits of constant depth with cn gates, but these techniques degrade and become no better than 2^n once the circuit size grows to roughly 4n or beyond for general (unrestricted-depth) circuits over B_2. No known algorithm improves on brute-force search for Circuit-SAT on general size-4n circuits; the question is widely cited as open in the circuit complexity literature.

status_evidence.title: The Complexity of Satisfiability of Small Depth Circuits
status_evidence.snippet: An improved randomized algorithm for satisfiability of constant-depth circuits with cn gates runs in time 2^{(1-δ)n}, with δ depending on c and depth d.
status_evidence.claim: Improved SAT algorithms exist for constant-depth linear-size circuits, but the improvement vanishes as size grows; no general improvement for size-4n unrestricted-depth circuits is known.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems (zbMATH 6986103)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists improving brute-force search for satisfiability of circuits of size 4n among the open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in the circuit complexity open-problems literature.
